before.title: Intratumoral cowpea mosaic virus immunotherapy for canine solid tumors
before.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
before.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page
before.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
before.funding: 🟢 Study-subsidized. The protocol brochure states that owners pay only for diagnostics, imaging, palliative care and other tests or care needed outside the study.
before.notes: The current Study 1 brochure explicitly includes mammary tumors alongside melanomas, soft tissue sarcomas, mast cell tumors and thyroid tumors. CPMV is injected weekly for one month before response evaluation; an additional month or subsequent therapy may be considered by the clinician. Off-study diagnostics, imaging and palliative care are owner-paid. Required on-study follow-up lasts at least three months.
before.special_requirement: Confirmed active melanoma, soft tissue sarcoma, mast cell tumor, thyroid tumor or mammary tumor accessible for intratumoral injection. No other chemotherapy or immunotherapy concurrently with CPMV; anesthesia and severe chronic disease risks require VROC screening.

before.title: CRT-Nanoparticle and HIFU Immunotherapy for Canine Melanoma
before.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page
before.intervention: Calreticulin nanoparticles plus HIFU, with or without anti-PD-L1
before.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
before.notes: Evaluates calreticulin nanoparticles plus HIFU, with or without anti-PD-L1, in dogs with melanoma.
before.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
before.funding: ⚪ Owner-paid. The protocol brochure states that owners fully pay for the study, although possible subsidies may be available.

before.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page
before.title: Radiation plus histotripsy for canine soft tissue sarcoma
before.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
before.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
before.funding: ⚪ Owner-paid. The protocol brochure states that owners fully pay for the study, although possible subsidies may be available.
before.notes: Open-label pilot treatment study combining radiation with image-guided histotripsy for naturally occurring canine soft tissue sarcoma. The registry describes radiation once weekly for three weeks with histotripsy twice weekly 24–72 hours after radiation, plus serial biopsies and monitoring.

before.title: Toceranib phosphate for metastatic, unresectable or recurrent canine insulinoma
before.center: UK multicenter study — Royal Veterinary College lead
before.status: Ongoing UK multicenter study — listed in the current ESVONC and Oncowaf trial directories
before.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with the participating center.
before.notes: Prospective treatment study comparing corticosteroids with corticosteroids plus toceranib, and surgery plus corticosteroids with or without toceranib, for metastatic/recurrent or unresectable canine insulinoma. The current Oncowaf listing names UK sites at RVC, Liverpool, Edinburgh, NDSR, Southfields and Dick White Referrals, plus a Netherlands site. Because the older RVC project metadata gave an end date of 31 May 2026, owners should still confirm that their preferred center is enrolling.

before.title: Oncolytic virus treatment access for canine osteosarcoma
before.center: Utrecht University Faculty of Veterinary Medicine
before.status: Study enrollment complete; treatment remains available for long-term research
before.contacts: Utrecht University Faculty of Veterinary Medicine — use the contact form on the official project page
before.funding: The January 2026 update says virus injections are free, but other treatment and research costs are not reimbursed or discounted.
before.notes: This is not an open clinical-trial enrollment: Utrecht says the study has enough participants. It remains listed as treatment access because dogs may still receive the viral therapy while contributing to long-term research.
